summary:
The clearest signal today is bullpen: all three ratings are riding identical 7-game winning streaks on bullpen picks, hitting 102-88 (54%, n=190) over the last 14 days, well above their season baselines near 50%. Pair that with SP, which is on a 5W streak across the board but actually cooling — R1, R2, and R3 are all sitting at 47-48% over the last 14 days on SP, a step down from season marks near 50%. R2's runs category is the one red flag in the model: COLD at -5.1pts versus baseline, sitting 89-101 (47%, n=190) with a live 4-game losing streak. Trust bullpen picks across all three ratings today, lean away from R2 runs, and treat SP as a category that's winning games but not covering at the rate its streak suggests.

The strong-play ledger is a season-long green light with a short-term warning sign — every rating is up big for the year (R1 +20.0u, R2 +20.0u, R3 +27.0u on n=274-304), but the last two windows have bled units across the board: R1 is -7.0u over 14 days and -4.0u over 7, R3 is -9.0u over 14 and -5.0u over 7, R2 is -8.0u and -5.0u respectively. This is a variance dip, not a structural break, given the season totals, but tighten stake sizing until the strong-play hit rate climbs back over 50%. On category combos, trends+runs remains the top play at 54.9% (228-187, n=415), with trends+sp and trends+bullpen close behind — anything trends agrees with is worth extra confidence. Team-wise, ride TBR when the model likes them: 24-10 (71%) overall and a blistering 18-5 (78%, +22.0u) on strong plays, the best combination of volume and edge on the board. LAD's strong-play mark (13-2, 87%, +16.0u) is even hotter on a smaller sample — worth a look if it lines up with a bullpen or trends signal. Fade HOU strong plays, which are bleeding at 3-8 (27%, -8.0u) despite a respectable 57% overall pick rate.
